findings.where: Screen 8 (400 V after five), hint for the 80 V answer
findings.what: The hint says 80 V 'splits 400 V into five equal drops', but five equal 80 V drops would leave 0 V; 80 V is 400 ÷ 5, so the hint describes a different slip from the one offered (say 'That divides 400 V by 5; each τ keeps 0.368 of what is left, five times over, 400 × 0.368⁵ ≈ 2.7 V').

findings.where: Screen 3 text and the explain's second paragraph
findings.what: 'Both slow it down and the pace is set by their product' skips the step that actually gives a product (both would also hold for R + C): the voltage falls at (v ÷ R) ÷ C = v ÷ RC volts per second, so at its starting pace, 10 V ÷ 47 s, it would be empty in exactly one RC, and because it slows it only reaches 0.368; one sentence would also show why RC is the unit of time.

The picture shows the effect (each bar × 0.368, R and C stretching the time axis) but not the cause, a fall rate in proportion to the gap; a short slope line or a 'falling at v ÷ RC V/s' readout at the handle would let him see half the gap fall half as fast.
On the 0 to 440 V scale the red 0 V ring sits on top of the true 2.7 V point (under 1 px apart), so the slip picture shows no difference; reuse screen 7's magnifier after an answer here.

findings.where: Screen 7 (Never quite full), opening demonstration at about 0.5 s
findings.what: The 95.0% label at 3τ vanishes with no fade as soon as the handle leaves 3τ, because labels between marks are dropped at once; fade it out like the others arrive.
The brief asked the screen to show where 99.3% comes from, 1 − e^(−5); the screen states 98.2% and 99.3% without their working (1 − e^(−4), 1 − e^(−5), or 0.368⁵ ≈ 0.007 left).

findings.where: Screen 7 text and the explain's third paragraph
findings.what: The 5τ convention is unsourced, although the brief names the trade tutorial (SECONDARY) for 99.3% at 5T and the 4.4 V worked example; the explain labels it 'textbooks add', but screen 7 states 'Engineers usually count 5τ as full or empty' with no label.

findings.where: Lesson as a whole, against the brief's row for lesson 3
findings.what: The brief's 'why it matters' line (a PFC capacitor bank must fall below 75 V within 3 minutes, IEC 60831 via a trade page) and Megger's insulation-test charging current that 'quickly falls to zero' are both missing; either would tie the curve to his trade.

findings.where: Screen 9 text and the explain's cooling paragraph
findings.what: 'Its own time constant ... is set by how much heat it holds and how easily heat leaves it' is true but neither cited nor labelled 'textbooks add', unlike the lesson's other uncited lines.

The finish says a discharge, a charge and a cooling part 'are the same shrinking gap', and screen 9 says the gap keeps 'the same share in each τ', both stronger than the explain's 'rougher fit' and 'roughly the same share'; say 'much the same' and give the limit on screen 9 as the brief asked.

The switch is offered but the screen has no time handle in any setting, so switching to discharging or charging only swaps the curve with nothing to step; hide the switch here, or let the cooling handle run after screen 10 has been answered.

90 to 120 words above the graph push the picture below the fold on a phone, so the 3 to 4.4 s demonstration plays before he scrolls down to it; Play again rescues it, but shorter screen text (the explain already carries the full reasoning) would read more calmly.
The gap bars are amber (fill2) while the brief's colour rule says ink for curves, bars and controls, with amber kept for key terms and what is due.
It says 'one time constant, written τ' without saying τ = R × C; until screen 3 only the header 'RC = 47 s' and the tick '1τ / 47 s' link the two, so add 'here R × C = 47 s'.
